display_name: Remote Patient Monitoring for Chronic Disease
description: Use of connected devices + symptom-logging apps + virtual check-ins to monitor patients with chronic conditions (T2D, HTN, CHF, COPD) and trigger care-team intervention on out-of-range readings. Domain studies whether monitoring reduces ER and hospital utilization, which patient segments benefit, and whether the per-patient program cost is justified by avoided utilization.
population: Adult patients with one or more chronic conditions, enrolled in a payer-funded or system-funded RPM program
research_questions: Does RPM enrollment reduce ER visits and hospitalizations vs. the year before enrollment?
Which patient segments (condition, age, baseline risk) benefit most?
Does patient engagement (readings, app use, completed care calls) predict outcomes?
Which clinic sites achieve the strongest outcomes, and what site-level factors explain the variation?
Does the per-patient program cost pay for itself in avoided utilization?
